page: Amazon Web Services r8a.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. Each core is backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache and 1 MB of L2 cache, complemented by 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is 32 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The instance carries a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps, includes zero integrated local storage, and features no dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-threaded compute efficiency. In Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests, the 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC architecture places the instance within the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, reaching a Geekbench single-core score of 2822.0. Single-threaded data throughput is similarly strong, registering 41.51 GB/s in gzip compression and 18.32 GB/s in bzip3 decompression. The processor also incorporates AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic accelerators (AES, VAES, SHA-NI), which drive top-tier generation throughput in lightweight language model inference (367.9 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model).

Across multi-core evaluations, the 4-core allocation yields expected mid-tier aggregate throughput, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 8882.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 13535.38. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 54.27 GB/s for large-block reads and 34.47 GB/s for large-block writes. Qualitative cost efficiency stems from its high single-thread clock speed paired with dense DDR5 memory allocation, allowing organizations to avoid overprovisioning core counts merely to meet specific memory footprints.

The primary operational tradeoff is the lack of bundled local NVMe storage and entry-level 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, requiring external block storage for persistent workloads. The r8a.xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive applications requiring strong per-core performance, such as in-memory caches, relational database hosting, medium-scale Redis deployments, data compression pipelines, and text-processing workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System, featuring a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs. Configured on the x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 32 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The hardware profile includes 16 MB of L3 cache, advanced instruction support including AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions, a 2 Gbps baseline network interface, and no attached local storage or GPUs. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier single-core performance alongside robust single-threaded compression and lightweight AI text-generation rates. With dedicated physical cores and high memory density per thread, the r8a.xlarge delivers cost-efficient resource allocation for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, web services, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines that require predictable per-core throughput without surplus core provisioning.
